source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check Storage controller information and detail information.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data readable/correct; storage controller status fits actual status; controller firmware version correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES reads a presumed ComputerSystem Storage collection as if it contained one flat `.StorageControllers` array and emits only Name/FirmwareVersion through a questionable jq expression. It omits Storage-member/controller-link traversal, RAID-versus-HBA role, PCIe/location identity, state/health, supported protocols/features and drive/volume relations.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly restores complete controller enumeration, topology, role, health, firmware and storage relations with a no-action boundary, but retains Pending for bounded Project topology and reference data.

old_problem: A controller name/version pair can appear correct while a second controller is missing, an HBA is misclassified as RAID, a PCIe device is mapped to the wrong slot, health is degraded, or firmware belongs to another controller. The prior review identified these risks but left the versioned controller inventory, roles and firmware matrix as an engineering decision.
disposition_reason: Traverse every Storage subsystem and its advertised modern Controllers collection or legacy StorageControllers representation, then bind each controller to the approved PCIe/physical/storage topology and role. Compare identity, RAID/HBA capabilities, live health, firmware and drive/volume relationships with the Project matrix and actual WebUI. The required inventory, role and target versions are deterministic configuration; inventory validation never authorizes RAID or firmware actions.
decision_basis: XLSX row 973, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 974 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 974 / variant 95653e0d7a4ec39c.

DMTF defines Storage collections, modern StorageController collections beneath each Storage resource and legacy embedded controller representations. Correct enumeration follows advertised schema/links and pagination rather than assuming `.StorageControllers` on the outer collection.

StorageController resources expose status, controller/device protocols and RAID capabilities; Project data supplies exact RAID/HBA role, physical/PCIe mapping, population, firmware target and acceptable relationship state.

The preceding drive testcase proves per-drive identity/status; it cannot replace this controller's own role, health, firmware, PCIe identity or association evidence, and this controller testcase cannot replace per-drive coverage.

ED-01, ED-08, ED-12, ED-13, ED-15, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 preserve RAID0 no-rebuild, visual/firmware evidence, SPEC-backed N/A and independent identity; ED-33 through ED-38 permit Project parameterization while prohibiting actions, log deletion, storage mutation, flash, reset/power and retry.

test_case.test_name: Validate every RAID/HBA controller's topology, role, health, firmware and storage relationships
test_case.purpose: Verify all Project-defined storage controllers are independently present at the correct physical/PCIe/Storage location, identified with the correct RAID or HBA role and supported protocols/features, healthy in the current configuration, running approved firmware, linked to the expected drives and volumes, and consistent with the actual BMC WebUI without invoking any controller or storage action.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/system/BIOS/storage/controller/WebUI identity and complete physical slot/BDF/PCIe-to-Storage-subsystem topology
Approved controller population matrix with manufacturer/model/part/serial correlation, RAID-versus-HBA role, controller/device protocols, supported capabilities and intended operating mode
Approved per-controller firmware authority and version target, including component identity rules for UpdateService or vendor inventory reconciliation
Expected controller-to-drive, enclosure, port and volume/array relationships plus status/health/cache/battery/foreign-configuration acceptance rules
Service-root-discovered ComputerSystem Storage collection, every Storage member and advertised modern Controllers or legacy StorageControllers representation with schema versions and pagination
Actual rendered WebUI storage-controller table/detail mapping, trusted TLS/protected credentials, identifier redaction, preserved logs and evidence storage
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY. Verify immutable target, discover the selected ComputerSystem Storage collection and enumerate every Storage member/page. For each member, follow the advertised modern Controllers collection and all pages, or parse the documented legacy StorageControllers representation according to `@odata.type`; preserve complete raw artifacts and ancestry. Bind every observed controller to the approved physical slot/BDF/PCIe device and Storage subsystem using durable links and protected stable identity, not name or array position. Record manufacturer/model/part/serial token, firmware version and authority, RAID/HBA role, Status.State/Health/Conditions, supported controller/device protocols and RAID types, PCIe/location/port data, cache/battery or foreign-configuration status when exposed, and linked drives/enclosures/volumes with timestamps. Capture the actual rendered WebUI controller list and every required detail and reconcile all fields/relationships with the Project matrix and preceding per-drive evidence without merging their verdicts. Preserve baseline/post SEL and audit evidence. Never follow Action targets. Do not clear logs, create/delete/modify/import/initialize/rebuild arrays or volumes, perform RAID0 rebuild, change mode/cache/policy, scan/reset a controller, flash firmware, reset/reboot or power-cycle.
test_case.expected_result: Every expected RAID/HBA controller is present exactly once at the approved physical/PCIe/Storage location with correct protected identity, role, protocols/capabilities, acceptable state/health and auxiliary status, approved firmware, and expected drive/enclosure/volume relationships. Unsupported functions are N/A only where the controller/Project specification proves that status. Modern/legacy API views and actual WebUI reconcile within freshness tolerance, and no controller, array, drive, volume or system state changes.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete Storage and controller traversal, topology-backed identity for every expected controller, explicit RAID/HBA role and capability checks, acceptable live status/health, authoritative firmware comparison, relationship reconciliation and actual rendered WebUI detail. Name/FirmwareVersion only, a flat embedded list, the preceding drive result or aggregate Storage health cannot pass. Missing/extra/duplicate/misplaced controller, wrong role/protocol/capability/firmware, degraded/stale state, unexpected relationship/configuration or UI/API/reference mismatch is FAIL. Missing topology, role, health rules or firmware target is NOT READY rather than Pending; unsupported/N/A is accepted only with authoritative SPEC evidence.
safety_gate: Use certificate-verified protected GET/read operations and target-advertised schemas/links; do not assume system ID, one Storage member or a universal embedded controller shape.
Bind each controller to physical slot/BDF/PCIe and storage topology through approved identifiers; display name, array order and shared firmware strings are insufficient.
Do not follow Redfish Action targets or vendor action links during inventory; preserve any advertised action metadata only as inert evidence.
Never rebuild RAID0 and do not create, delete, initialize, import, clear, rebuild, expand or modify any array/volume, drive relation, controller mode, cache or policy.
Preserve logs before deletion; prohibit controller rescan/reset, firmware upgrade/downgrade, BMC/system reset or reboot and all power transitions.
Stop on incomplete traversal, ambiguous identity, degraded/stale health, foreign configuration or mismatch; do not auto-retry through reset, rescan or power cycle.
expected_evidence: Immutable target/schema/WebUI identity and approved physical/BDF/PCIe/Storage controller population, role and firmware matrix
Complete paginated Storage members and modern controller members or legacy controller payloads with ancestry, timestamps and hashes
Per-controller matrix with protected identity, location/BDF, RAID/HBA role, protocols/capabilities, status/conditions, firmware authority/value and verdict
Controller-to-drive/enclosure/port/volume relationship graph and explicit cache/battery/foreign/N/A policy results where applicable
Actual rendered WebUI controller table/detail visual artifacts with API/UI/reference and separate drive-case reconciliation
Preserved pre/post logs, inert-action/no-RAID/no-flash/no-reset/no-power proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is intended. On an unknown controller, topology ambiguity, foreign/degraded state, firmware uncertainty or relationship mismatch, stop and preserve/redact API, UI and log evidence for the storage owner. Do not clear logs, follow actions, import/clear/rebuild/change RAID or HBA state, reset/rescan a controller, flash firmware, reset/reboot, power-cycle or automatically retry.

source_conflict.reason: The Master consistently requires controller detail, actual status and firmware. DeepSeek's name/version-only flat query is incomplete guidance, not an alternate requirement.

blocked.reason: Read-only RAID/HBA controller inventory/status/firmware validation is standard and technically defined. Exact controller topology, roles, relationships and accepted firmware/health data are finite Project prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Physical/BDF/PCIe/Storage controller topology and population; RAID/HBA roles/capabilities; actual modern/legacy schema; health/cache/battery/foreign rules; drive/volume relationships; per-controller firmware authority/targets; WebUI mapping; trust and redaction.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; READ-ONLY STORAGE CONTROLLER REVIEW ONLY; NO API, WEBUI, ACTION, LOG CLEAR, RAID/HBA, CONTROLLER RESET, FLASH, RESET, POWER OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

Those versioned inputs make passive controller verification deterministic without authorizing configuration or flash.
